items.title: George "Pops" Foster and Mugsy Spanier Interview, 1957-04-21
items.q: When did you make those records with Mackenzie Condon? ... I just made one record with Eddie and the... It was one record then? Yeah.

ctx.x: Well, the chordal rhythm came from the Memphis Ennis band. Like when they had roast beef tuxedo and tuxedo and said, you know, you ought to see myth. That was the biggest thing about Memphis is a myth. You know, I got it from the second line, send me the... I give it to myth. Myth said, this is the one he never did good. Let's see it. When did you make the music?

When did you make those records with Mackenzie Condon? That was a little later, huh? Uh-huh. I just made one record with Eddie and the... It was one record then? Yeah. Be some changes made, found a new baby. That's the only one I made. I didn't make sugar and all that. You mean you just made two sides? That's it? That's all. Yeah. Then later when I went to New York or I made two, I made some. The Blue Busters. And what was life like for a musician in Chicago in the 20s? Very good then. Everything. If you couldn't…

Chicago was the number one spot for musicians in the St. Louis. Chicago was St. Louis. They had both fun on in the St. Louis. But then they, and the general, they had St. Louis over. Then you go to the Beardstown, Beardstown, man. Quite a few spots. Used to take us there. Where was that? Illinois. Who had St. Louis sold up? John Rowland who? No, General Hogan as a gangster. Oh. And Danny Colbeck.
